artifacts.summary: Designs the /slice build task set: six new records, two description revisions, fifteen edges, with every ordering claim and file-state figure re-derived from the live state and source store.

memory_candidates.content: A decision record's 'ordered after nothing; it has no caller' claim about a deletion successor goes stale the moment a sibling task that was meant to be revised closes as written instead. Before siting a deletion task as independent, re-run grep -rl for the doomed file's name over the source store: a caller added after the ruling (and context docs re-pointed to cite the file as the live implementation) turns an independent deletion into one ordered after the task that removes the caller.

update-task-status.sh can add a dependency edge (preflight <dependent> edge_only <session> --depends-on-add='[N]', dependent is the positional number, cycle-refused at write time) but has no edge-removal flag. Removing an edge is a state-write.sh jq filter of the shape (.active_projects[] | select(.project_number == N) | .dependencies) |= (. - [A, B]). An edge onto an abandoned-and-archived task dangles (the predecessor is no longer in active_projects), while an edge onto a completed task is merely satisfied.
